# Sequence and flowchart gaps found while writing skills/siren

## Problem

Writing `skills/siren` measured five places where the renderer disagrees with its own docs or
with Mermaid 11.17.2 (nook issues 01M3NK0C1, 01M3NK0C6, 01M3NK0CB, 01M3NK0CH, 01M3NK408). The
skill currently tells authors to route around each of them.

## Outcome

Each gap is closed, observable through `render()` or the default theme, and the skill's
workaround text for it is gone.

## Scope

1. **01M3NK0C1** — A `timeline:` block can name a sequence diagram's notes (`note:N`) and
   activation bars (`activation:N`).
2. **01M3NK0C6** — `highlight X outline` visibly changes every sequence-diagram target.
3. **01M3NK0CB** — Every sequence-diagram keyword is matched case-insensitively (widened from
   `note` alone; see Domain decisions).
4. **01M3NK408** — The flowchart `click X "url"` shorthand accepts an optional tooltip and
   target, and a flowchart click tooltip is drawn.
5. **01M3NK0CH** — A participant referenced before any declaration is created implicitly, as
   Mermaid does.

## Non-goals

- `title: Hi` (colon form), `links A: {json}`, the mermaid-probe `Option` global, and keyword
  case in the other four diagram kinds. Each becomes its own backlog issue.
- Recoloring a message's arrowhead on `outline` (flowchart edges don't either).
- Any change to `siren-board`.

## Domain decisions

- **Timeline targets (0C1).** `note:N` and `activation:N` are timeline targets in a sequence
  diagram, as CONTEXT.md already states. Ids are unchanged: notes numbered in source order,
  activation bars by one shared counter assigned when a bar opens.
- **Outline on sequence targets (0C6).** Outline recolors to `--siren-highlight-color` and
  thickens to `--siren-highlight-stroke-width`, as in every other kind:
  - participant: both participant-row boxes (or actor figure), the lifeline (stays dashed) and
    the destroy mark — every element wearing the id (ADR-0009);
  - message: the line only, never the shared arrowhead marker;
  - block: its frame and dividers; `rect`: a stroke added to its existing fill rectangle, no
    new element;
  - box: its background frame; activation bar: its rect; note: already covered.
- **Keyword case (0CB).** Every sequence keyword is case-insensitive, with Mermaid's meaning:
  `participant`, `actor`, `as`, `title`, `accTitle`, `accDescr`, `link`, `loop`, `alt`, `else`,
  `opt`, `par`, `and`, `critical`, `option`, `break`, `rect`, `end`, `box`, `create`,
  `destroy`, `activate`, `deactivate`, `autonumber` (and `autonumber off`), `note`, and the
  positions `left of` / `right of` / `over`. `note LEFT OF A` draws on the left.
- **Click shorthand (408).** `click X "url" ["tooltip"] [target]` produces exactly the
  interaction `click X href "url" ["tooltip"] [target]` does. A flowchart node's tooltip is
  drawn as a leading `<title>` child of the node group, the convention the class and sequence
  renderers already use. Siren keeps emitting `target` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- **Implicit participants (0CH).** Reverses the explicit-reference rule (sequence slice spec;
  its premise "mirror flowchart's no implicit node creation" is false — flowchart creates
  nodes implicitly):
  - a message (either end), note, `activate`, `deactivate` or `destroy` naming an undeclared
    participant creates it, with no diagnostic;
  - lane order is first-mention order across declarations and references, in flattened
    statement order (block bodies included);
  - a later `participant X as Label` / `actor X` for an already-mentioned X applies its label
    and type retroactively and does not move X;
  - `create participant X` after X was mentioned stays an error (Mermaid rejects it);
  - an implicitly created participant is never in a `box`; box members are declarations, so
    the "box groups undeclared participant" check is removed.
  Recorded as ADR-0013; CONTEXT.md updated.

## Design contract

No new public interface. All behavior lives behind the existing seams.

### `render(source, container, options?)` (siren-core)

- Responsibilities: parse, model, lay out, draw; report every problem as a `Diagnostic`.
- Invariant kept: problems in a document come back as diagnostics, never thrown.
- Observable through: `SirenRenderResult.diagnostics`, `data-siren-id` / `class` / attributes
  on the returned `svg`, and element classes after `controller.next()`.

### Default theme (`theme/default.css`)

- Responsibilities: every visual rule, including the highlight effects.
- Observable through: `getComputedStyle` on rendered elements in jsdom with the theme
  injected, before and after adding `siren-highlight-outline` (the existing pattern in
  `theme/default.test.ts`).

### Compatibility corpus (`compat/corpus.ts`)

- Each newly supported Mermaid construct gets a `supported` row whose `assert` reads the
  rendered SVG. Ratchets in `corpus.test.ts` must keep passing.

## Acceptance criteria

See each ticket. Shared by all five:

- [ ] The skill text that routes around the gap is removed or corrected (named per ticket).
- [ ] `packages/core/CHANGELOG.md` gains a line under `[Unreleased]` (Fixed or Added).

## Test strategy

- Seam: `render()` and the default theme, as above; corpus rows for Mermaid compatibility.
- Test type: integration through `render()` in jsdom (vitest), plus corpus rows.
- Dependency handling: all in-process and real; no mocks.

## Verification

- Focused: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run <test file>`
- Suite: `pnpm test` (repo root; runs siren-core and siren-board)
- Static: `cd packages/core && npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`
- Skill examples: after a ticket touches `skills/siren`, every example block in
  `skills/siren/SKILL.md` and `references/syntax.md` still validates (see ticket notes).
- E2E: None.

## Baseline

Measured at de0f7ff on 2026-09-29: `pnpm test` passes (siren-core 1418 tests / 35 files,
siren-board 33 / 2); `tsc --noEmit` clean in both packages. No known failures.

## Risks and deferred questions

- 0CB touches every sequence regex; a lowercase-only assumption elsewhere (e.g. a keyword
  compared with `===` after matching) could survive. The corpus rows exercise each keyword.
- 0CH changes lane order for documents that mention a participant before declaring it; any
  existing test pinning the old error will change by design.
- `demos/sequence-diagram.html` prose refers to "Retry at step 4"; 0C1 must append its new
  step after the existing ones.
